text:
maya: proposing a new synthetic traffic pattern for benchmarking — 'staggered Laplace spikes' to emulate sudden user-driven microbursts with long-tail latency impact
aj: concise — can you sketch the shape?
lina: curious how this differs from our sawtooth/burst generator
maya: idea: base QPS ramp + periodic clusters where spike amplitude follows a Laplace (double-exponential) distribution, staggered across hosts to create infra-level contention knobs. helps exercise KV cache churn + kernel switch thresholds
aj: ok, practical params?
maya: here's a minimal config prototype:
```
pattern: staggered_laplace
base_qps: 50
spike_period_s: 120
spike_duration_s: 4
spike_location_lambda: 0.6  # controls tail heaviness
stagger_hosts: true
stagger_ms: 250
kv_warmup: true
```
devon: neat. For apples-to-apples we should pin model/checkpoint + quantization and disable server-side autoscale during runs :thumbsup:
aj: add explicit kernel-selection toggle too — we need to toggle between default kernel picker and forced kernel to measure selection overheads
lina: also track: batching stats (avg batch size, batch wait), kv hit/miss, kernel-switch count, tail p99/p999 latency. capture traces for any spike regressions
maya: agreed. Expected failure modes: 1) KV cold miss storm causing token amplification 2) kernel-switch thrash when bursts push sequence len distribution over threshold 3) batching heuristic increasing latency by greedy batching during brief spikes
samir: question — how do we ensure the generator is reproducible? stochastic spikes sound non-deterministic
maya: seedable RNG and deterministic host staggering. Also store the generated QPS trace and replay it via our harness for exact replays
aj: can we run a small pilot tonight on staging? I can drop a gated job that runs 10x 4s spikes over 20 minutes against a 4-GPU pool
perf-bot: scheduled job #perf/1765432199-pilot started (staging cluster). will post artifacts to /artifacts/1765432199/ when done
devon: measurement checklist before pilot:
- freeze model revision / quant config
- set autoscale=off
- enable perf counters (kernel selection, batch stats)
- run baseline (steady qps) for 15m
- run staggered-laplace for 20m
- collect traces and compare p50/p95/p99/p999 and kernel-switch histogram
aj: running baseline now
perf-bot: baseline complete. p99=120ms, p999=420ms, avg batch size=6. artifacts: /artifacts/1765432199/baseline.json
maya: starting the staggered Laplace run. seeding=42, stagger_ms=250
perf-bot: run complete. artifacts: /artifacts/1765432199/staggered_run.json
aj: quick scan: p99 jumped to 190ms, p999 to 980ms. kernel-switch count spiked 3x during bursts. batch wait increased from 6ms to 28ms peak
lina: looks like the batching heuristic is waiting too long for coalescing during the 4s spikes — maybe threshold should be adaptive by instantaneous QPS estimate rather than fixed window
samir: KV miss rate also rose from 2% to 14% during the second-half spikes — cold prefixes + stagger caused eviction thrash
maya: action items:
- aj to reproduce with forced kernel (disable dynamic selection) to see if switch cost is dominant
- devon to run with aggressive KV prefetch/warmup to test miss mitigation
- lina to prototype adaptive batch timeout based on rolling QPS estimate
- samir to run replay of the recorded trace later for regression suite
aj: I'll run forced-kernel and upload results to the same artifact path by EOD
perf-bot: noted. tagging run as regression-candidate if p999 > 2x baseline
maya: thanks all. this pattern caught a combo of batching + kv + kernel interaction which we hadn't seen in isolated tests — good candidate for adding to our standard perf matrix
devon: +1, we should also add a 'stagger factor' sweep to see at what stagger_ms value the effects maximize
lina: will prototype adaptive timeout tomorrow
samir: I'll queue the replay job after aj's forced-kernel run finishes
maya: closing loop: update the harness doc and add example config to repo once we have the forced-kernel and warmup runs attached. :rocket:
